Must include at least one semester of English composition/literature. Up to two semesters of AP or IB credit may be applied if courses deemed acceptable by your undergraduate institution.

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: The USC School of Medicine Greenville is deeply committed to fostering a culture of fairness, equity and inclusion among our diverse students, faculty, staff and other key stakeholders. The Student Advocates for Diversity, Inclusion, and Equity (SADIE) exists as a body of welcoming students, faculty and staff committed to: advancing the integration of diversity and inclusion within the medical school’s curriculum; supporting those student organizations with an emphasis on diversity; and fostering an environment for meaningful discussions centered on diversity and inclusion at USC School of Medicine Greenville. The Levi S. Kirkland Society Mentoring Program and the Hispanic Medical Society offer a faculty-student paired mentoring program for students who identify as Black/African American, Hispanic/Latinx, and/or Native American. Additional organizations that work to support the needs of our diverse student body are listed above in the Student Organizations and Activities section.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Students may request a Leave of Absence through the Associate Dean for Student Affairs and Admissions.  The Associate Dean will guide the student through the process.  The Dean will meet with the student, consider all information and will inform the student in writing of the decision regarding the request and the process of appeal.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities:
The USC School of Medicine Greenville's Office of Student Affairs provides support for student organizations, societies and extracurricular and community-based activities to meet the interest of our student body. Our students work with the Office of Student Affairs to establish and coordinate activities such as community engagement and service, intramural sports, student leadership development programs, specialty interest groups, intercultural student organizations and interprofessional student experiences. 

Additional organizations that work to support the needs of our student body include the Student National Medical Association (SNMA), Latino Medical Student Association (LMSA), Asian Pacific American Medical Student Association (APAMSA),  the Global Health Interest Group, LGBTQ Health Interest Group, and the Medical Student Pride Alliance (MSPA). MSPA is the first chapter of the Medical Student Pride Alliance in South Carolina and was founded in 2020.
medSchoolStudLife.setting:
The USCSOM Greenville is located in the Upstate of South Carolina, in the foothills of the Blue Ridge Mountains. Greenville, SC offers beautiful natural attractions and a vibrant downtown with hundreds of diverse restaurants and shops and the 32-acre Falls Park; diverse cultural experiences (e.g. music, theater, street festivals, art galleries); and a 22-mile multi-use greenway along the Reedy River. In 2020, Greenville, SC was rated by Condé Nest Traveler as the Friendliest City in the U.S. 

The center of activity at the School of Medicine is the 90,000-square-foot School of Medicine Building, located on the Greenville Memorial Medical Campus of Prisma Health. This facility was designed around our integrated curriculum and features a spacious patio, outdoor amphitheater and convenient on-site parking garage. It also houses student services offices, common areas for study and social gatherings, and innovative learning spaces designed to enhance the educational program.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: On-campus housing is not available.  The University of South Carolina School of Medicine--Greenville Office of Student Affairs maintains a listing of area apartments and houses available for rent.  Rent averages around $1,000 - $1,200 per month.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: The Medical Student Pride Alliance (MSPA) is an activist and social organization committed to empowering sexual and gender minority medical students and allies and increasing the number of physicians trained in LGBTQ-inclusive healthcare. The LGBTQ Health Interest Group is committed to promoting the health and well-being of LGBTQ students and patients by educating future and current healthcare providers through focus groups, panel discussions, case presentations and literature reviews. The LGBTQ Health Interest Group aims to foster healthy dialogue between colleagues of all backgrounds and engage in conversations regarding health of sexual and gender minority communities with the LGBTQ Alliance of our partner health system, Prisma Health, which was developed to promote equality and visibility for gender and sexual minorities at Prisma Health. The LGBTQ Alliance prioritizes provider clinical education, staff sensitivity training, and development of a supportive clinical environment.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: The USC School of Medicine Greenville works closely with the Student Disability Resource Center to provide appropriate and feasible accommodations for students.  Students must be able to meet the school's technical standards for admission.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: The USC School of Medicine Greenville is dedicated to helping you maintain a healthy lifestyle and our location on the Prisma Health medical campus gives you easy access to outstanding fitness and health care facilities and services.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: The USC School of Medicine Greenville is a place where students learn using the latest clinical, information and simulation technology and where they develop the leadership, clinical and interpersonal skills essential to delivering the next generation of patient-focused health care with confidence and compassion.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: On campus housing is not available. Students who do not have transportation will have to find transportation to and from campus.  During M3 and M4 years, students will be expected to go to their various clinical rotations therefore transportation is highly recommended.
medSchoolStudLife.additionalSupportProgrameName: Our SASS Team identifies opportunities for growth in each medical learner, skill cultivation, and attends to a student’s inner self so they are empowered during their journey in medicine.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Students are expected to dress in a professional manner at all times.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Faculty office hours are available to students throughout the modules.  Peer tutoring is available on a small group or individual basis upon request. Academic success coaches are assigned to students.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: EMT training begins on the first day of classes and presents the student with patient interactions.  Patient interactions are integrated throughout the curriculum beginning early in the first year.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Curriculum integrates the basic and clinical sciences with a graduated increase in clinical skills and responsibilities across the four years of the curriculum.  Small group and lecture-based courses.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Clinical rotations begin at the start of the M3 year.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Due to the interactive nature of the curriculum, students are expected to attend select lectures and all small group sessions on a punctual and regular basis.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: The M.D. program at the University of South Carolina School of Medicine Greenville is a unique journey into the world of medicine that begins with hands-on clinical training as Emergency Medical Technicians, and continues through exploration of the scientific, social, clinical and cultural facets of the profession.  The integrated curriculum offers a  blend of interactive experiences from classroom to bedside that are designed to foster and enhance the acquisition of essential knowledge, communication, diagnostic and problem-solving skills, and leadership skills in clinical and community-based settings. USC School of Medicine Greenville focuses on student-centered learning as the roadmap for the life-long learning continuum from undergraduate to graduate and continuing medical education.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: Our goal is to educate master clinicians imbued with medical knowledge, committed to care of the total patient, competent in technical skills, and cognizant of population health principles. Our graduates will be committed to evidence-based, cost-effective, patient-centered care using a professional philosophy which stresses constructive communication and inter-professional team-based care. Constantly attuned to community and societal needs, USC School of Medicine Greenville will train inquisitive physicians who take responsibility for the healthcare needs of the diverse communities they serve.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: As a “Different School of Thought”, we view research as applying scientific rigor to fill a knowledge gap, catalyze discovery, advance health equity, or change health care delivery to improve quality, cost, and access. USCSOMG has a Research Scholars Program that will allow students to apply for a funded research program to begin between their M1-M2 year. In addition, she is working with our community to launch the Student Catalyst Fund which will sponsor research projects, national organization engagement and student travel. Future plans also include an innovator/entrepreneurial internship and health policy internship. Through our unique partnership with Prisma Health, Clemson, Furman and USC scientists and clinicians, we are thrilled to provide our students with unique avenues to engage in research, ignite inquiry, develop as change leaders, and contribute to discoveries for a healthier South Carolina and nation.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Following EMT Certification, a monthly shift is required during the first 2 years.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Research is optional for students, but many students participate in research projects.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: Clinical rotations are performed at hospitals and community-based medical practices throughout Prisma Health's network of healthcare centers.
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: Pass/Fail in Biomedical Science courses and Integrated Practice of Medicine and Elective Courses for M1 and M2.  M3 and M4 Clerkship and Acting Internships have a letter grading system.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: The University of South Carolina School of Medicine - Greenville received preliminary accreditation from the Liaison Committee on Medical Education in October 2011.  The School of Medicine Greenville is a separately accredited school from the University of South Carolina School of Medicine in Columbia, SC.  The innovative educational program blends interactive experiences on a unified campus of state-of-the-art classrooms, Clinical Skills and Simulation Center, and patient encounters at Greenville Memorial Medical Campus of Prisma Health.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
Mission:  Educate. Innovate. Serve.  
Where Lifestyle is Medicine.

Vision:  USC School of Medicine Greenville empowers the next generation of physicians through cutting-edge technology, interprofessional collaboration, innovative teaching, and transformational research. We strive to educate compassionate future physician leaders to deliver the highest quality patient care, enhancing the health and wellness of the communities we serve.

medSchoolApplication.cbcRequired: All accepted applicants to USCSOM Greenville will be subject to a criminal background investigation. Offers of admission are contingent upon satisfactory criminal background investigation results.
medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: Please note, unofficial recommendation letters will not be received or taken into consideration during the evaluation of applicants. Only Letters of Recommendation submitted through an applicant’s AMCAS application will be considered
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: We require at least three letters of recommendation, with a maximum of five letters. If your undergraduate institution prepares a premedical advisory committee letter, we will accept that to fulfill the minimum letter requirements. We will not consider letters written by individuals who are personally related to you, such as family members or close friends, and instead we require letters from professional contacts who can objectively evaluate your academic and clinical abilities, such as professors, research advisors, or supervising physicians. Please see the AAMC Guidelines for writing letters of recommendation.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: One virtual traditional 50-minute interview with 2 members of the Admissions Evaluation Committee
medSchoolApplication.edpAvailableTxt: The EDP gives applicants the opportunity to secure an acceptance from one medical school by October 1, while still allowing sufficient time to apply to other schools if not accepted.
medSchoolApplication.ctsRequired: We do accept non-resident applications. Approximately 30% of each incoming class is comprised of non-resident students.
medSchoolApplication.stateResAfterMatric: Out-of-state students have the option to establish SC state residency during their first year of medical school so they can pay SC resident tuition rates for years 2, 3 and 4.
medSchoolApplication.acceptOutstateApplInformation: Each incoming class has approximately 30% of students who come from out-of-state
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
Pass/Fail Coursework & Online Coursework and Labs - For students who do not receive grades during this semester, we will accept pre-requisites as pass/fail courses and online labs to meet the requirements if they were taken during a semester when your University offered online-only schedules for health and safety reasons.
•	Letters of Evaluation - During our evaluation of applicants, we will remain cognizant of the fact that clinical and observation experiences may be more difficult to obtain during this application cycle. 
•	MCAT - We will continue to require an MCAT score to receive a secondary application and/or to be offered an interview.  However, for those who wish to retake the MCAT after an initial score, we will accept MCAT scores through February 2026 (the MCAT must be taken by January 2027) if additional MCAT dates are not offered after September 2026.
•	Choose Your Medical School Tool - We encourage students to select Plan to Enroll by May 15, 2027 and require require students to select Commit to Enroll by June 8, 2027.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: The Admissions Committee at USCSOMG considers the highest MCAT score within the past 3 years of an application cycle.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo: We do not have a minimum MCAT score requirement. However, the average MCAT score for matriculating students is typically around the 82nd percentile.
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo: We do not have a minimum GPA  score. However, the average GPA for matriculating students is typically 3.7-3.75.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: All postbacc and graduate coursework will be considered
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: There is no minimum number of credit hours.  All postbacc and graduate coursework will be considered
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: The Admissions Committee will look for evidence demonstrating your ability to successfully complete rigorous academic material.  The Admissions Committee prefers that all recruited coursework be completed at a 4 year accredited university but will consider coursework taken at a community college.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo:
You are welcome to supplement your application with additional information. Our Admissions Evaluation Committee will consider your updates along with the review of your application. 

We ask that you only submit updates that are significant and relevant to your application.

Application updates may be made in AMP under the Document Upload Tab

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid:
Loan programs and scholarships are available for entering students. Our financial aid officer advises new and current students on loan opportunities and debt management. Part-time employment while in medical school is not possible. 

The Scholarship Committee considers both financial need and academic merit in the awarding of scholarships.
medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy: Tuition is determined annually by the University of South Carolina's Board of Trustees.   The current policy allows out-of-state students to apply for South Carolina residency and pay in-state tuition for years 2, 3 and 4 of medical school.

medSchoolTimeline.eventDetail: 'Commit to Enroll' must be selected by students accepted to University of South Carolina School of Medicine Greenville no later than 21 days prior to Orientation.

medSchoolMdPathway.programDesc: The Primary Care Accelerated Track (PCAT) at the University of South Carolina School of Medicine Greenville is a three-year MD pathway designed for students committed to a career in primary care. This program offers an innovative three-year curriculum, a seamless transition into one of three Prisma Health Family Medicine residency programs, and a full-tuition scholarship in exchange for a four-year service commitment following residency.
medSchoolMdPathway.eligibleApplicants: Applicants who are admitted into the traditional 4-year program at USCSOMG can be considererd for the PCAT program if interest is indicated.
medSchoolMdPathway.applicationDeadline: Same as the Regular Decision AMCAS Application Deadline: November 1st
medSchoolMdPathway.applicationProcess:
Individuals should complete their AMCAS application and submit to USCSOMG. Applicants indicate interest in PCAT for Family Medicine by answering additional questions in the supplemental application sent to you by the Admissions Office.
After earning acceptance to USCSOMG, PCAT applications will be evaluated by affiliated Family Medicine Residency programs. Applicants may be invited to a virtual interview with the PCAT leadership team.  Notifications go out in the Spring of the application year
medSchoolMdPathway.programRestReq: Applicants must be admitted into the traditional 4-year program to be considered.  Otherwise there are no additional restrictions.
medSchoolMdPathway.residencyAffiliationPathway: Directed residency option for all Three-Year MD students
medSchoolMdPathway.resAdditionalInfo:
Who Should Apply?
Candidates who have:
Demonstrated interest in a Family Medicine career
Commitment to community health and wellbeing
Desire to complete residency in one of the three Prisma Health Upstate Residency Programs
Ability to commit to employment with the Prisma Health organization for 4 years after completion of residency

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistInformation: This number varies from year to year
medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: The waitlist will be established in March after all interviews are completed.  Not all applicants who interview are placed on the waitlist.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
Required:
Two semesters of biology with lab
Two semesters of general (inorganic) chemistry with lab
One semester of organic chemistry with lab (a second semester of organic chemistry with lab is only required if it is a prerequisite for biochemistry)
One semester of Biochemistry; lab is not required
One semester of physics with lab
Three semesters of humanities, social and behavioral sciences to include at least one semester of English composition/literature.

Recommended:  Cell biology, Genetics
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: While there is no timeframe in which students must meet the prerequisite coursework, competitive applicants will have recent exposure and demonstrate in-depth competency in the required prerequisites.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: The Admissions Committee uses a thorough approach to select applicants who have achieved  academic excellence, bring a variety of characteristics and experiences, and who exhibit exceptional interpersonal and communication skills, integrity, honesty, empathy, a propensity for teamwork, maturity, emotional stability, leadership, a strong work ethic, self-direction, and demonstrated  passion for becoming a doctor.  Prior to extending an offer to interview, the Admissions Committee will evaluate previous academic performance to include undergraduate GPA and MCAT scores, letters of recommendation, clinical and research experience, work and volunteer experience, leadership roles, unique accomplishments, grit, long term goals and extracurricular activities.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: The Admissions Committee strongly recommends that all applicants gain shadowing or another type of clinical experience prior to applying to our medical school.  Applicants should be able to demonstrate clinical insight throughout their AMCAS and Supplemental Applications.  If selected for an interview, applicants will be expected to provide examples of clinical experiences in order to demonstrate their knowledge of the field, their passion for medicine and their compassion for future patients.
